layers.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India (e-FRRO portal)
layers.process: The area between the Inner Line and the international border is a Protected Area (Third Schedule). The Order traces the line along high ridges and rivers, including the Bhagirathi, Alaknanda, Dhauli Ganga and Gori Ganga, from Singa Ghati to the Kali and Gori Ganga junction on the Nepal border. Foreigners need a Protected Area Permit beyond it. Apply online at indianfrro.gov.in (the e-FRRO portal) or in the Indian Visa Su-Swagatam app; the permit is issued electronically. Citizens of Afghanistan, China or Pakistan, and people of origin there (born there, a parent or grandparent born and permanently living there, or ever a citizen), need the central government's prior approval. Smartraveller advises applying at least 4 weeks ahead; entering without a permit carries significant penalties.

layers.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India (e-FRRO portal)
layers.process: Listed Tibetan settlements, monasteries and institutions in and around Dehradun are Restricted Areas (Fourth Schedule): among them Clement Town (including Mindrolling and Tashi Kyil monasteries), Sahastradhara, Manduwala, Herbertpur and Lakhanwala, Nalapani, and the Sakya Centre and Tibetan Women Centre on Rajpur Road. Daytime visits are allowed without a permit if the settlement, monastery or institute gives the visitor's name, parentage, date of birth, nationality, passport and visa numbers to the Foreigners Registration Officer. Staying needs a Restricted Area Permit; foreign students can get one valid for 3 years if the institute vouches for them.

laws.rule: Corbett Tiger Reserve requires an official registered guide on every excursion; visitor entry permits are obtained at reception and are not transferable.
laws.heading: Corbett Tiger Reserve visitor rules

laws.rule: At Corbett Tiger Reserve visitors must not enter restricted zones or drive off designated routes. Driving in the reserve after sunset and entering the national park after sunset are prohibited.
laws.heading: Corbett Tiger Reserve visitor rules

laws.rule: At Corbett National Park and the Dhikala and Bijrani tourist complexes, cooking is not allowed. At other rest houses, visitors may cook in the space provided.
laws.heading: Corbett Tiger Reserve visitor rules

laws.rule: At Corbett, day visits to the Dhikala tourism zone are permitted only on conducted tours organised by the reserve. Private buses may not enter Bijrani tourism zone.
laws.heading: Corbett Tiger Reserve visitor rules

laws.rule: Corbett Tiger Reserve prohibits lighting fires, and requires guests to obtain a clearance certificate before leaving their accommodation inside the reserve.
laws.heading: Corbett Tiger Reserve visitor rules

laws.rule: Corbett Tiger Reserve prohibits smoking outside residential complexes and rest houses.
laws.heading: Corbett Tiger Reserve visitor rules

laws.rule: Pets are not permitted inside Corbett Tiger Reserve. Visitors must not tease, chase or attempt to feed animals.
laws.heading: Corbett Tiger Reserve visitor rules

laws.rule: Corbett Tiger Reserve requires visitors to carry a litter bag and take non-biodegradable litter back out. Littering outside bins is subject to penalties.
laws.heading: Corbett Tiger Reserve visitor rules

laws.rule: Corbett Tiger Reserve prohibits firearms and playing radios or tape recorders within the reserve.
laws.heading: Corbett Tiger Reserve visitor rules

laws.rule: Corbett Tiger Reserve prohibits blowing horns and driving above the posted speed limit.
laws.heading: Corbett Tiger Reserve visitor rules

laws.rule: At Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary or its tourism zone, walking, trekking and getting out of a vehicle are prohibited except at designated places; visitors may not enter restricted zones.
laws.heading: Guidelines to be followed by Tourists

laws.rule: At Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary, cooking is prohibited except at designated places without a canteen; lighting fires is prohibited.
laws.heading: Guidelines to be followed by Tourists

laws.rule: The Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary tourist guidelines prohibit smoking in public places and during sanctuary or tourism-zone excursions.
laws.heading: Guidelines to be followed by Tourists

laws.rule: At Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary visitors must carry a litter bag and take non-biodegradable waste outside the forest; they must not chase, tease or feed wildlife.
laws.heading: Guidelines to be followed by Tourists

laws.rule: At Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary or its tourism zone, driving outside prescribed times or routes, sounding horns and exceeding the speed limit are prohibited.
laws.heading: Guidelines to be followed by Tourists

laws.rule: Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary prohibits carrying or consuming alcoholic beverages in the sanctuary or tourism zone.
laws.heading: Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary visitor guidelines

laws.rule: Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary guidelines prohibit carrying and using intoxicants, drugs and narcotics in the sanctuary or tourism zone. Ask the sanctuary directly about necessary prescribed medicines.
laws.heading: Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary visitor guidelines

laws.rule: Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary prohibits taking pets into the sanctuary or tourism zone.
laws.heading: Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary visitor guidelines

laws.rule: A valid sanctuary permit is required to use a route through Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary to reach nearby religious places; follow the permit’s stated timing and conditions.
laws.heading: Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary visitor guidelines

laws.rule: For routes to religious sites through Nandhaur Wildlife Sanctuary, the guidelines prohibit movement after sunset and restrict heavy vehicles, including tractor-trolleys, on routes specified for Byandhura Temple, Kaladev Temple and Reetha Sahib Gurudwara.

laws.rule: Under the Uttarakhand Protection of Cow Progeny Act 2007, section 5, no one may keep in possession, sell or transport beef or beef products in any form. Beef means the flesh of cow progeny (a cow, bull, bullock, heifer or calf). Taking cow progeny out of the State needs a permit, for rearing and protection only, with a fee of INR 500 per animal (about A$7).
laws.penalty_signal: Sections 3 and 5: 3 to 10 years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine of INR 5,000 to 10,000 (about A$75 to A$149) (section 11(1)). Offences are cognizable and non-bailable.

laws.rule: The Uttarakhand Anti Littering and Anti Spitting Act 2016 (sections 3 and 4) makes it an offence to throw or leave litter, including bottles, cans, food wrappers and food, or to spit, in any public place. Public place expressly includes a hill side, road, park and lane. The Act applies in areas run by urban local bodies (municipalities).
laws.penalty_signal: The State sets the fine (section 9). An authorised officer can offer to compound the offence for up to INR 500 (about A$7), and a person who cannot pay may do community service instead (section 10).

laws.rule: The Uttarakhand Plastic and Other Non-biodegradable Garbage (Regulation of Use and Disposal) Act 2013 bars throwing non-biodegradable garbage, or food waste in a plastic bag, into drains, ponds, streams or rivers (section 4(1)); bars leaving garbage in a public place except in a closed receptacle or a designated spot (4(2)); and bars burning non-biodegradable garbage (section 5). Section 3 lets the State restrict or ban plastic items by notification.
laws.penalty_signal: Up to 3 months of simple imprisonment or a fine of up to INR 500 (about A$7) for an individual (section 10); double for a repeat offence.
